documents.title: Developing course policies around A.I.
documents.stance_why: The CTT page says the faculty senate requires an AI statement in every syllabus but 'It is entirely up to the individual instructor to determine which policy to use', and it offers three example categories (permitted/encouraged, allowed under specific circumstances, prohibited). The document sets no stance of its own, so delegates with tiers listed.
documents.summary: The Center for Transformative Teaching explains that UNL's faculty senate requires an AI policy in every syllabus and leaves the content to instructors. It gives considerations for choosing a policy, advice on communication and citation, and example policy language in three categories plus mixed-use classes.

units.why: The page states the faculty senate rule that every syllabus must carry an AI policy, which is a requirement on instructors about communicating expectations (type P09 'Require an AI statement in every syllabus').
units.anchor: requires that you incorporate a policy related to AI use into your syllabus
units.policy: The faculty senate at UNL requires instructors to incorporate a policy related to AI use into their syllabus.

units.why: 'It is entirely up to the individual instructor to determine which policy to use' leaves the choice of AI rule to each instructor, so P04 (instructor sets the rule).
units.anchor: It is entirely up to the individual instructor to determine which policy to use

units.why: 'it is essential that you clearly explain to students what the expectations are' obliges instructors to communicate AI expectations, matching P09 (state expectations to students).
units.anchor: it is essential that you clearly explain to students what the expectations are around AI

units.why: 'no one-size-fits-all approach' says the right AI rule differs by course, so decisions sit at the course level (P04).
units.anchor: There’s no one-size-fits-all approach here since courses differ vastly from one another

units.why: The warning that students 'may assume that the rules from their other courses also apply in yours' is the reason a course's AI policy must stay course-specific, so P11 (each course's policy governs only that course).

units.why: 'violations of your course AI policy should be treated the same as any other academic integrity violation' routes AI misuse into the ordinary misconduct process, P36.

documents.title: AI and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: The page states 'instructors are allowed to set their own course policies regarding AI use' and that the Code of Conduct treats unauthorized AI as cheating unless the instructor gives permission. It does not itself set a permit or ban, so delegates.
documents.summary: The page explains that UNL's Student Code of Conduct was amended to cover work prepared by 'an entity', so unauthorized AI use counts as cheating or plagiarism. It describes the three-step process, the reporting duty, why AI checkers are not provided, and signs instructors may weigh as evidence.

units.why: 'the best evidence often comes from the intuition you have as an instructor' with listed signs sets what evidence to weigh, P69.
units.anchor: the best evidence often comes from the intuition you have as an instructor
units.fit_note: P69 includes statements that hunches are not enough; this page treats instructor intuition as the best evidence.

units.why: 'Language too advanced or specialized for the nature of the assignment' is a listed sign of AI use, P69.
units.anchor: Language too advanced or specialized for the nature of the assignment

units.why: 'Using obscure, irrelevant, or non-existent references' is a listed sign, with the advice to require 'a direct link to all references', P69.
units.anchor: Using obscure, irrelevant, or non-existent references

units.why: 'requiring students to include a direct link to all references' is a suggested assignment requirement that helps catch fabricated sources, P35.
units.anchor: requiring students to include a direct link to all references
units.fit_note: A requirement added to assignments to support checking, not a full redesign.

units.why: 'A writing style that significantly differs from other work submitted in class' is a listed sign, P69.
units.anchor: A writing style that significantly differs from other work submitted in class

units.why: 'collecting an in-person writing sample early in the semester' supplies a baseline for comparison, P40 (process evidence).
units.anchor: collecting an in-person writing sample early in the semester
units.fit_note: A baseline writing sample, not similarity software or commit logs.

units.why: 'if you meet with the student and have an attitude of genuine support, the student will admit' frames a supportive meeting as the route to admission, close to presuming good faith, P68.
units.anchor: if you meet with the student and have an attitude of genuine support
units.fit_note: Frames a supportive meeting as the route to admission, close to presuming good faith.

notes: Coder A. Example syllabus language on the CTT page is coded as units because it is the university teaching center's own sample policy text, with actor student. No school, computing or course documents were collected for this university.
